summary:
MARS-X – Martian Exploration & Survival Guide is an interactive web-based platform designed to support safer and smarter human and robotic exploration of Mars. The project aims to simplify complex Martian environmental data and transform it into meaningful insights for mission planning and exploration.

The platform integrates multiple exploration features, including an interactive Mars dashboard, 3D planetary visualization, geological exploration, atmospheric and radiation analysis, landing site safety assessment, rover subsystem information, and route planning. These features help users understand Martian terrain, environmental challenges, potential hazards, and suitable exploration regions.

MARS-X focuses on addressing critical challenges associated with Mars missions, such as extreme environmental conditions, radiation exposure, terrain uncertainty, and navigation risks. By presenting exploration information through an accessible and interactive interface, it helps users visualize mission conditions and make informed decisions.

Developed during the NASA Hackathon, MARS-X combines web technologies, scientific information, and interactive visualization to create an engaging Martian exploration experience. Ultimately, the project aims to contribute to the understanding of planetary exploration and support future mission planning for safer exploration of the Red Planet.
